<security_assessment>
<decision>UNSAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains a critical security issue in the `prepare()` function where it downloads and executes a binary (Bazel) from GitHub's release page without any integrity verification. Specifically, it fetches `bazel-${bazel_version}-linux-x86_64` using `wget` and immediately makes it executable with `chmod +x`, then adds it to the PATH for use in the build process.

This constitutes a supply-chain attack vector because the downloaded Bazel binary is not verified against a checksum or signature. The version is dynamically read from the `.bazelversion` file in the source tree, meaning an attacker who compromises the upstream repository could silently redirect the build to use a malicious version of Bazel, which would then execute with full privileges during the build phase. Since this binary runs arbitrary code as part of the build system, it could exfiltrate build secrets, modify output binaries, or compromise the entire build environment.

While the rest of the packaging logic is standard (patching, version setting, wheel building), the lack of verification for a downloaded and immediately executed binary from an external source elevates this to an unsafe practice that undermines the integrity of the package.
</details>

</details>
